headings: Overview: Our Mission is to Make Biology Easier to Engineer
1.Biology is programmable. All living things run on the same DNA code.

2.Biology matters. The ability to engineer biology has had and will have a profound impact on how we develop new medicines and vaccines, grow our food, and manufacture many of the things we use every day.
3.Biology is hard. Today, it is still too difficult and too costly to engineer biology, preventing critical innovations from reaching the market.
Cell Engineering: enabling the discovery, functional optimization and efficient manufacturing of biotechnology products

paragraphs: Unless the context otherwise requires, all references in this section to the "Company," "Ginkgo," "we," "us," or "our" refer to the business of Ginkgo Bioworks Holdings, Inc. and our subsidiaries.

Our mission is to make biology easier to engineer. That has never changed. Every choice we've made with respect to our business model, our platform, our people, and our culture is grounded in whether it will advance our mission.

Ginkgo sells services to government and commercial customers in two business segments: cell engineering, where we provide tools and biological R&D services across a range of industries, and biosecurity, where we provide services to customers who are working to identify, monitor, prevent, mitigate, and ultimately protect humanity from biological threats. An overview of these two business segments is provided below.
Our cell engineering customers work with biology to discover and manufacture new products that have transformative potential across industries:
•in medicine, developing innovative new therapeutics and vaccines; •in agriculture, advancing the sustainability and security of our food systems;
•in industrial biotechnology, advancing the way we manufacture a wide range of products for better performance and lower environmental impact; and
•in government, advancing new R&D priorities of strategic importance to the United States and its allies.

Because engineering biology is difficult and unpredictable, biotech R&D is traditionally performed by in-house labs filled with highly trained scientists running lab experiments by hand over several years in the hope of ultimately developing a working product. Many cell engineering projects fail in development due to scientific challenges, and many are terminated because they are taking too long or are over budget.

Ginkgo does not make end products; instead, we offer biological R&D services on our platform to enable our customers to bring their products to market. Historically, Ginkgo's primary service offering has been cell engineering R&D services (solutions) where Ginkgo performs technical activities. In 2024, Ginkgo expanded its service offering to include services that provide our customers cell engineering tools for biological R&D, where Ginkgo enables its customers to conduct certain in-house R&D activities themselves. Our services are designed to offer customers better results on the dimensions of probability of success, speed, or cost – and ideally on all three.

The fundamental advantage of our cell engineering platform over traditional cell engineering done by hand at our customers' labs is that our platform improves with scale while in-house cell engineering in our customers' labs largely does not. Compounding and mutually reinforcing improvements of our laboratory automation and software infrastructure—our Autonomous Lab—and our reusable data assets enable us to improve our services with each successive project.

Our Autonomous Lab is a flexible wet lab built from our Reconfigurable Automation Cart ("RAC") systems capable of large scale data generation; it powers generative AI and machine learning ("ML") tools that enable more successful biological R&D. We now offer services providing such data generation, AI and automation tools directly to Ginkgo customers. Our data assets comprise best practices for cell engineering, along with sequences and host cells that have been honed through dozens of programs and can be directly reusable for our cell engineering solutions. We now offer licenses to our host cells and other IP assets, such as our broad metagenomic library.

Cell engineering service offerings, depicted on a spectrum of customization and technical risk borne by Ginkgo on the vertical axis, and the mix of up-front service fees and downstream value we charge on the horizontal axis.

In every technological revolution, reaping the benefits to the economy and society requires grappling with the corresponding risks. A critical part of making biology easier to engineer is creating robust biosecurity infrastructure to help manage the many accelerating and diversifying sources of biological risk, whether natural or engineered, accidental or malicious.

In the digital world, we've learned that we need to build comprehensive infrastructure to protect our digital systems —from financial markets to power grids—from harmful code. The modern cybersecurity industry offers tools to constantly identify, monitor, prevent, and mitigate cyber risk in near real-time. This is happening constantly, all around us. Our physical world demands the same type of widespread biosecurity infrastructure to detect, characterize, respond to, attribute, and prevent biological threats.

You should carefully consider the following risk factors, together with all of the other information included in this Annual Report, before making an investment decision. Our business, prospects, financial condition or operating results could decline due to any of these risks and, as a result, you may lose all or part of your investment.
Unless the context otherwise requires, all references in this section to the "Company," "we," "us" or "our" refer to the business of Ginkgo and its subsidiaries.

We have incurred significant operating losses since our inception. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of approximately $6.2 billion. We may incur losses and negative cash flow from operating activities for the foreseeable future as we continue to invest significant additional funds toward further developing our platform and customer offerings, the cell engineering programs we perform on behalf of our customers and otherwise growing our business, including our Biosecurity and Automation business units. We have derived a significant portion of our revenues from fees and milestone payments from technical development services provided to customers to advance programs, as well as a significant portion of our revenues from Biosecurity. Historically, these fees have not been sufficient to cover the full cost of our operations. Additionally, if our customers terminate their agreements or development plans with us, our near-term revenues could be adversely affected. In addition, certain of our customer agreements provide for milestone payments, future royalties and other forms of contingent consideration, the payment of which are uncertain, as they are dependent on our ability to successfully develop engineered cells, bioprocesses, or other deliverables and our customers' ability and willingness to successfully develop and commercialize products and processes.

Our expenses may continue to exceed revenues in the foreseeable future and we may not achieve profitability. If we fail to achieve profitability, or if the time required to achieve profitability is longer than we anticipate, we may not be able to expand or continue our business, and the value of our common stock could be negatively impacted. Our ability to achieve or sustain profitability is based on numerous factors, many of which are beyond our control, including the development of our platform, the initiation of new programs with new and existing customers, the commercial terms of our programs, the realization of any potential downstream value from our programs, our ability to advance cell engineering programs in a timely and cost-effective manner, our ability to extend new offerings to customers, our customers' ability to scale up bioprocesses, the ability of our customers to produce and sell products, the impact of market acceptance of our customers' products, and our customers' market penetration and margins. Even if we do achieve profitability, we may not be able to sustain or increase profitability on a quarterly or annual basis.

We have consumed considerable amounts of capital to date, and we expect to incur continued net losses for the foreseeable future as we continue to develop our business, advance our programs, expand and enhance our platform and customer offerings, perform on behalf of our customers, and make the capital investments necessary to scale up our business. We have used, and may continue to use, additional capital for Biosecurity, strategic investments and acquisitions. We believe that our cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, and interest earnings will be sufficient to meet our projected operating requirements until we reach profitability. However, these assumptions may prove to be incorrect and we could exhaust our available capital resources sooner than we currently expect. Because of the numerous risks and uncertainties associated with our programs, including risks and uncertainties that could impact the rate of progress of our programs, we are unable to estimate with certainty the amounts of capital outlays and operating expenditures associated with these activities.

We do not currently have any commitments for future funding. We may receive fees, milestones, and royalty payments under our customer agreements, but these are not guaranteed. We have received non-cash consideration in the past and we may receive additional non-cash consideration in the future where we may not be able to realize the eventual cash proceeds expected or at all such that the amount of cash proceeds eventually realized may be less than the revenue recognized and the costs incurred to perform those services. Additionally, we may wish to sell our equity interests in certain subsidiaries or collaborations but most of these equity stakes are in private companies and we may not be able to find a buyer due to contractual restrictions or otherwise, or may incur significant impairment if we sell these positions for liquidity. We may not receive any further funds or future non-cash consideration under those agreements, the funds or non-cash consideration we receive may be lower than projected and/or disclosed as potential downstream value, or our program costs may be higher than projected. In addition, we may not be able to sign new customer agreements or enter into new development plans with existing customers with adequate funds to cover program development expenses. As a result of these and other factors, we do not know whether additional financing will be available when needed, or, if available, whether such financing would be on terms favorable to our stockholders or us.

Ginkgo sells services to government and commercial customers in two business segments: cell engineering, where we provide tools and biological R&D services across a range of industries, and biosecurity, where we provide services to customers who are working to identify, monitor, prevent, mitigate, and ultimately protect humanity from biological threats. An overview of these two business segments is provided below.

Ginkgo does not make end products; instead, we offer biological R&D services on our platform to enable our customers to bring their products to market. Historically, Ginkgo's primary service offering has been cell engineering R&D services (solutions) where Ginkgo performs technical activities. In 2024, Ginkgo expanded its service offering to include services that provide our customers cell engineering tools for biological R&D, where Ginkgo enables its customers to conduct certain in-house R&D activities themselves. Our services are designed to offer customers better results on the dimensions of probability of success, speed, or cost – and ideally on all three.

The fundamental advantage of our cell engineering platform over traditional cell engineering done by hand at our customers' labs is that our platform improves with scale while in-house cell engineering in our customers' labs largely does not. Compounding and mutually reinforcing improvements of our laboratory automation and software infrastructure—our Autonomous Lab—and our reusable data assets enable us to improve our services with each successive project.

Our Autonomous Lab is a flexible wet lab built from our Reconfigurable Automation Cart ("RAC") systems capable of large scale data generation; it powers generative AI and machine learning ("ML") tools that enable more successful biological R&D. We now offer services providing such data generation, AI and automation tools directly to Ginkgo customers. Our data assets comprise best practices for cell engineering, along with sequences and host cells that have been honed through dozens of programs and can be directly reusable for our cell engineering solutions. We now offer licenses to our host cells and other IP assets, such as our broad metagenomic library.

We charge customers fees for the services we provide in our cell engineering tools offerings. Fees for our automation solutions (RAC systems) are typically earned over a period that covers design, build, and deployment and range from six to twelve months. In addition, we offer support services for our RAC systems with fixed fees covering the support periods.

Fees for our Datapoints services are typically earned over a shorter period of time (weeks to months) than for cell engineering solutions, which may be multi-year programs. A typical deliverable for a Datapoints program is a data package. Fees for cell engineering solutions programs are typically structured as a fixed fee for a fixed scope of work.

Our cell engineering solutions are typically scoped and delivered as a program ranging in duration from several months to several years. A typical deliverable for the program would comprise an enzyme sequence, or an engineered strain or cell line and its associated bioprocess. For each of these programs, we generate economic value in two primary ways.

First, we charge service fees for Autonomous Lab services, in much the same way that cloud computing companies charge usage fees for utilization of computing capacity or CROs charge for services. R&D is inherently risky and our customers recognize that this is a cost they will incur regardless of success and whether they are working on the program in-house or with a partner. Typically, service fees for a program include a fixed fee for a fixed scope of work and may also include payments contingent upon hitting certain technical milestones. If we are able to deliver program results with less work through the use of Codebase assets and/or generative AI tools, then we can achieve the same revenue with lower cost or in
a shorter duration. Service fees provide a strong foundation of revenue that is independent of any commercialization efforts by our partners.

Second, as the key enabling technology for our customers' products, we have historically negotiated a value share with our customers (in the form of royalties, milestones, and/or equity interests) in order to align our economics with the success of the programs enabled by our platform. Because we typically do not incur material downstream costs (e.g., manufacturing or product development, which our customers manage), these value share payments flow through with approximately 100% contribution margin. We have structured a variety of value sharing mechanisms, including royalties, lump-sum milestones, and equity payments. As Ginkgo has matured, we have shifted our downstream value towards milestone payments and commercial royalties rather than equity. In addition, commencing in the second quarter of 2024, we announced changes in prospective commercial terms, including the removal of downstream value share from certain program types.

This flexible business model allows for more predictable near-term revenue in up-front research fees and technical milestones without sacrificing our ability to create long-term value with asymmetric upside through downstream value share (typically in the form of a royalty stream, milestone, and/or equity share). As we add more programs to the platform over time, we expect downstream value share to contribute income, which could in turn grow our overall margins and cash flow profile for our cell engineering solutions. The realization of potential revenue related to downstream value in the form of potential future milestone payments and royalties and/or equity consideration is dependent upon a number of factors, including our ability to successfully develop engineered cells, bioprocesses, data packages, or other deliverables, and the product development and commercialization success of our customers.

paragraphs: 除非文意另有說明，本節所有提及「本公司」、「Ginkgo」、「我們」、「我們」或「我們的」均指 Ginkgo Bioworks Holdings, Inc. 以及我們的子公司之業務。
我們的使命是讓生物學更容易進行工程設計。這一點從來沒有改變。我們在商業模式、平台、人才以及文化方面的所有選擇，都是基於是否能促進我們的使命。
Ginkgo 向政府與商業客戶銷售服務，業務分為兩個應報告分部：在細胞工程分部，我們提供跨多個產業的工具與生物研究發展服務；在生物安全分部，我們為致力於識別、監測、預防、緩解並最終保護人類免受生物威脅的客戶提供服務。以下為這兩個應報告分部的概要說明。
我們的細胞工程客戶與生物學合作，以發現並製造具有跨產業變革潛力的新產品：
•在醫療領域，開發創新性新藥物與疫苗；•在農業領域，推進我們糧食系統的可持續性與安全性；
•在工業生物技術領域，推進我們製造廣泛產品的方式，以實現更好的性能與較低的環境影響；以及
•在政府領域，推進對美國及其盟友具有戰略重要性的新研究發展優先事項。
由於工程生物學困難且難以預測，傳統的生物科技研究發展通常由內部實驗室進行，這些實驗室由高度專業的科學家組成，他們透過手動進行實驗室實驗，耗時數年，以期最終開發出可行的產品。許多細胞工程專案在研發階段因科學挑戰而失敗，許多則因耗時過長或超支預算而中止。

Ginkgo 並不製造最終產品；相反地，我們透過我們的平台提供生物研究與開發服務，以協助客戶將其產品推向市場。歷史上，Ginkgo 的主要服務為細胞工程研究與開發服務（解決方案），其中 Ginkgo 進行技術活動。2024 年，Ginkgo 擴展其服務範疇，包含提供客戶細胞工程工具的服務，以協助客戶自行進行部分內部研究與開發活動。我們的服務設計為讓客戶在成功機率、速度或成本等維度上獲得更優的結果，理想情況下是在這三個維度上都有所提升。
我們的細胞工程平台與傳統由客戶實驗室手動進行的細胞工程相比，其根本優勢在於我們的平台會隨著規模擴張而提升，而客戶實驗室內的細胞工程則基本上不會。我們實驗室自動化與軟體基礎設施—我們的自主實驗室（Autonomous Lab）—以及可重複使用的數據資產的累積與相互強化改進，使我們能透過每個後續專案來提升我們的服務。

我們的自主實驗室（Autonomous Lab）是一個靈活的濕實驗室，由我們的可重新配置自動化推車（Reconfigurable Automation Cart，簡稱 RAC）系統組成，能夠進行大規模數據生成；它驅動生成式人工智能（Generative AI）與機器學習（Machine Learning，簡稱 ML）工具，使生物研究與開發更加成功。我們現在提供服務，直接向 Ginkgo 客戶提供此類數據生成、人工智能與自動化工具。我們的數據資產包含細胞工程的最佳實踐，以及透過數十個專案磨練出的序列與宿主細胞，可以直接用於我們的細胞工程解決方案。我們現在提供對我們宿主細胞及其他智慧財產權資產的授權，例如我們廣泛的元基因組庫。
細胞工程服務範疇，以 Ginkgo 承擔的客製化程度與技術風險為垂直軸，以及我們收取的前期服務費用與後續價值為水平軸的光譜圖。
在每一次科技革命中，要讓經濟與社會受益，必須面對相應的風險。讓生物學更容易工程化的一個關鍵部分，是建立強韌的生物安全基礎設施，以協助管理許多加速與多樣化的生物風險來源，無論是自然或工程製造、意外或蓄意的。
在數位世界中，我們學會了需要建立全面的基礎設施，以保護我們的數位系統—從金融市場到電力網—免受有害程式碼的影響。現代的網路安全產業提供工具，以近乎即時的方式持續識別、監測、預防與緩解網路風險。這正在持續發生，就在我們周圍。我們的實體世界同樣需要這種廣泛的生物安全基礎設施，以偵測、鑑定、回應、歸因並預防生物威脅。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應配合本年度10-K表報表所附之合併財務報表及其相關附註一併閱讀。此外，本10-K表之此部分一般討論2025年與2024年項目及2025年與2024年之間的年度比較。關於2023年項目及2024年與2023年之間的年度比較，若未包含於本10-K表中，請參閱我們2024年10-K表之第二部分，第7項「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」，該文件已於2025年2月25日提交美國證券交易委員會。

請參閱本 Form 10-K 所包含之內容，請參閱我們 2024 年 Form 10-K 中 Part II, Item 7. 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析，該文件已於 2025 年 2 月 25 日向美國證券交易委員會提交。本討論包含向前看的陳述，反映我們的計畫、預估與信念，這些陳述涉及風險與不確定性。實際結果可能與這些向前看陳述中預期的有重大差異，原因可能是許多因素，包括在本年度報表 Form 10-K 其他部分所討論的 Item 1A. "風險因素" 以及 "向前看陳述之警示說明"。

Ginkgo為政府與商業客戶提供兩大業務分部的服務：細胞工程，我們提供跨多個產業的工具與生物研究發展服務；以及生物安全，我們為致力於識別、監測、預防、緩解並最終保護人類免受生物威脅的客戶提供服務。以下為這兩個業務分部的概要說明。

Ginkgo並不製造最終產品；相反地，我們透過平台提供生物研究發展服務，協助客戶將其產品推向市場。歷來，Ginkgo的主要服務為細胞工程研究發展服務（解決方案），其中Ginkgo執行技術活動。2024年，Ginkgo擴展其服務，包含提供客戶細胞工程工具以進行生物研究發展的服務，讓客戶能自行進行部分內部研究發展活動。我們的服務設計為讓客戶在成功機率、速度或成本等維度獲得更佳結果，理想情況下是在這三個維度都獲得改善。
我們的細胞工程平台與傳統由客戶實驗室手動進行的細胞工程相比，根本優勢在於我們的平台隨著規模擴張而提升，而客戶實驗室的內部細胞工程則 largely 不具此特性。我們實驗室自動化與軟體基礎設施—我們的自主實驗室（Autonomous Lab）—以及可重複使用的數據資產的累積與相互強化改進，使我們能隨著每個後續專案提升服務。

我們的自主實驗室（Autonomous Lab）為一個靈活的濕實驗室，由我們的可重新配置自動化推車（Reconfigurable Automation Cart，簡稱RAC）系統組成，能進行大規模數據產生；它驅動生成式人工智能與機器學習（Machine Learning，簡稱ML）工具，使生物研究發展更為成功。我們現已提供服務，直接向Ginkgo客戶提供此類數據產生、人工智能與自動化工具。我們的數據資產包含細胞工程的最佳實務，以及透過多個專案磨練出的序列與宿主細胞，可直接用於我們的細胞工程解決方案。我們現已提供對我們宿主細胞及其他智慧財產權資產（如我們廣泛的元基因組庫）的授權。
我們向客戶收取我們在細胞工程工具服務中所提供的服務費用。我們自動化解決方案（RAC系統）的費用通常在設計、建造與部署期間內分期確認，範圍從六到十二個月不等。此外，我們也提供RAC系統的支援服務，以固定費用覆蓋支援期間。
我們 Datapoints 服務的費用通常在較短的時間內（數週至數個月）產生收入，與 cell engineering 解決方案相比，後者可能是跨年度的計畫。一個 Datapoints 計畫的典型交付成果是一組資料包。cell engineering 解決方案計畫的費用通常以固定費用為主，並針對固定的服務範圍進行結構化。
我們的 cell engineering 解決方案通常以計畫形式進行規劃與交付，計畫的持續時間從數個月到數年不等。一個典型計畫的交付成果通常包含一個酵素序列，或一個工程化菌株或細胞株及其相關的生物製程。對於這些計畫，我們透過兩種主要方式創造經濟價值。

首先，我們為 Autonomous Lab 服務收取服務費用，與雲端計算公司收取計算資源使用費用或 CROs 收取服務費用的方式類似。研發本質上具有風險，而我們的客戶認知到這是一項他們無論計畫是否成功，或是在內部進行或與合作夥伴進行，都必須承擔的成本。通常，一個計畫的服務費用包含固定費用，並針對固定服務範圍，也可能包含達成特定技術里程碑的付款。如果我們能透過 Codebase 資產和/或生成式 AI 工具，以較少的工作完成計畫結果，則我們可以以較低的成本或較短的時間實現相同的收入。
服務費用為我們提供一個強固的收入基礎，與我們合作夥伴的商業化努力無關。

其次，作為我們客戶產品的關鍵啟動技術，我們歷來與客戶協議價值分享（以版稅、里程碑和/或股權形式），以使我們的經濟效益與我們平台所啟動的計畫的成功程度一致。由於我們通常不會產生重大後續成本（例如製造或產品開發，這些由客戶管理），這些價值分享付款的毛利約為 100%。我們已建立多種價值分享機制，包括版稅、一次性里程碑付款和股權付款。隨著 Ginkgo 的成熟，我們已將後續價值轉向里程碑付款和商業版稅，而非股權。此外，自 2024 年第二季起，我們宣佈了未來商業條款的變更，包括從某些計畫類型中移除後續價值分享。

這種靈活的商業模式使我們能在前期研究費用和技術里程碑中獲得更可預測的短期收入，而不影響我們透過後續價值分享創造長期價值的能力（通常以版稅流、里程碑和/或股權分享形式）。隨著我們逐步增加更多計畫至平台，我們預期後續價值分享將產生收入，這可能進而提高我們 cell engineering 解決方案整體的毛利和現金流表現。與後續價值相關的潛在收入，以未來可能的里程碑付款和版稅及/或股權形式實現，取決於多種因素，包括我們成功開發工程化細胞、生物製程、資料包或其他交付成果的能力，以及我們客戶的產品開發和商業化成功程度。

headings: 與本公司業務相關的風險
本公司有淨虧損的歷史。我們預期在可預見的未來會持續產生虧損，且我們可能永遠無法達成或維持獲利。
我們未來可能需要大量額外資金以支應業務運作。
我們曾經歷過顯著的組織變革，若我們未能有效管理這些變革，則可能對本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
本公司有限的營運歷史及不斷演進的業務，使評估目前業務及未來前景變得困難。
對生物安全服務需求的不確定性可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
本公司可能涉及證券或股東訴訟及其他相關事項，這些事項可能耗費大量金錢與時間。此類訴訟及相關事項可能對本公司業務造成損害。
本公司持有其他營運公司股權及其他非現金對價，因此面臨價格波動及流動性風險。
我們運用自身資源，並與策略性及財務投資者合作，以協助早期階段公司與創新者取得資金，並受益於我們的平台，這使我們面臨許多風險。
我們可能無法完成未來的策略性併購，或成功整合策略性併購，這可能會對我們的業務與財務狀況造成不利影響。
我們使用生物、危險、易燃及/或受管制的材料，這些材料需要相當的訓練、專業與費用才能處理、儲存與處置，並可能導致對我們提出索賠。
第三方可能使用我們的工程細胞、材料與生物體以及相關的生產流程，以可能損害我們聲譽的方式進行。
我們業務的國際擴張使我們面臨在美國境外進行業務所涉及的業務、法規、政治、運營、財務與經濟風險。
我們在人工智能的投資與應用可能導致聲譽損害、責任或對我們業務運作產生其他不利後果。
與我們客戶相關的風險
我們的營業收入集中於極少數的客戶，其中一些為關聯企業，若失去重要客戶，我們的營業收入、營運成果、現金流量與聲譽可能會受到影響。

paragraphs: 投資本公司證券涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列風險因素，並配合本年度報告中所包含的所有其他資訊，再做投資決定。本公司業務、前景、財務狀況或營運結果可能因這些風險而惡化，因此您可能損失全部或部分投資。
除非文意另有明確要求，否則本節所有提及「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」或「我們」的參考，均指 Ginkgo 及其子公司之業務。

自我們成立以來，我們已產生顯著的營運虧損。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累計虧損約為 6.2 十億美元。我們可能在可預見的未來持續產生虧損及營運活動產生的負現金流，因為我們持續投入大量資金用於進一步發展我們的平台與客戶產品、為客戶執行的細胞工程計畫，以及其他業務擴張，包括我們的生物安全與自動化業務單位。我們的收入有相當大一部分來自於為客戶提供技術開發服務以推進計畫所收取的費用與里程碑付款，以及來自生物安全的收入。歷來，這些費用並不足以覆蓋我們全部的營運成本。此外，如果我們的客戶終止與我們的契約或開發計畫，我們的短期收入可能會受到不利影響。此外，我們某些客戶契約中提供里程碑付款、未來版稅及其他形式的或有對價，其支付具有不確定性，因為這些支付取決於我們成功開發工程細胞、生物製程或其他交付成果的能力，以及客戶成功開發與商業化產品與製程的意願與能力。

我們的費用可能在可預見的未來持續高於收入，我們可能無法實現盈利。如果我們無法實現盈利，或實現盈利所需時間長於預期，我們可能無法擴張或持續經營業務，本公司普通股的價值可能會受到負面影響。我們實現或維持盈利的能力取決於許多因素，許多因素超出我們的控制範圍，包括我們平台的發展、與新舊客戶啟動新計畫、我們計畫的商業條款、我們計畫潛在下游價值的實現、我們能否以具成本效益的方式及時推進細胞工程計畫、我們能否向客戶推出新產品、客戶能否擴大生物製程規模、客戶能否生產與銷售產品、客戶產品市場接受度的影響，以及客戶的市場滲透率與利潤率。

我們迄今已消耗大量資金，且我們預期在可預見的未來持續產生淨虧損，因為我們持續發展業務、推進計畫、擴張與增強平台與客戶產品、為客戶執行工作，並進行必要的資本投資以擴大業務規模。我們已使用，且可能持續使用額外資金用於生物安全、戰略投資與收購。我們認為我們的現金及現金等價物、短期投資與利息收入將足以應付我們預期的營運需求，直到我們實現盈利為止。然而，這些假設可能證明是錯誤的，我們可能比預期更快耗盡可用資金。由於與我們計畫相關的許多風險與不確定性，包括可能影響計畫進度的風險與不確定性，我們無法確定這些活動所需的資金支出與營運支出金額。

我們目前沒有任何未來資金的承諾。我們可能根據客戶契約收取費用、里程碑付款與版稅，但這些並非保證。我們過去曾收到非現金對價，我們未來也可能收到額外非現金對價，但我們可能無法實現預期的現金進帳，甚至完全無法實現，因此最終實現的現金進帳可能低於已確認的收入與執行這些服務所產生的成本。此外，我們可能希望出售某些子公司或合作夥伴的股權，但這些股權大多屬於私人公司，我們可能因契約限制或其他原因無法找到買家，或出售這些股權時可能產生重大減值。我們可能無法根據這些契約獲得進一步資金或未來非現金對價，我們獲得的資金或非現金對價可能低於預期與披露的潛在下游價值，或我們的計畫成本可能高於預期。此外，我們可能無法簽訂新客戶契約或與現有客戶簽訂新開發計畫，以足夠資金覆蓋計畫開發費用。由於這些及其他因素，我們無法確定是否在需要時能獲得進一步融資，或如果能獲得，是否在對股東或本公司有利的條件下進行。
